question: What claim about the uniqueness of this knowledge is at stake in asserting that nothing equal to it will exist again?
premises: Knowledge equal to this is in view.
Such knowledge will not exist again.
Nor will it exist in the future at all by this measure.
inference: No knowledge equal to this knowledge exists or will exist again.
uncertainties: The scope of 'again' is not specified by this verse alone.
plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there be again.
